Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our Privacy and Procurement teams:

1) For our UK patients data (production workloads), do you consider the standard EU SCCs sufficient when combined with your technical safeguards, or do we need the separate UK IDTA / UK Addendum as a mandatory contract for UK-resident data?

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Brooks <daniel.brooks@medtechinc.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data routing and transfer controls for UK operations

Hi Daniel — thanks for the DPIA and straight questions. Short answer up front:

- For EU transfers: the EU SCCs (2021 module-based clauses) plus our documented technical/organizational safeguards are sufficient in most cases.
- For the UK: we recommend the UK IDTA / Addendum be executed in addition to the SCCs when (a) the data subject population is primarily UK-resident or (b) your legal team requires explicit UK-specific model clauses.
- TIAs: yes — any subprocessor sending data to a third country with elevated risk will trigger a narrow Transfer Impact Assessment (we run a shortform TIA per subprocessor and can share the findings).

Practical next steps we suggest:
1) Redwood prepares a draft IDTA (attached: uk-idta-draft.docx) and our current subprocessor map (redwood_subprocessor_map.csv).
2) We run a quick subprocessor scan against your DPIA and produce short TIAs for any implicated subprocessors (48–72 hours).
3) Legal review + redline window (MedTech counsel) — targeted 7 business days.
4) DocuSign execution + implementation (we can target a two-week calendar from final redlines if nothing material is open).

Estimated calendar (assuming IDTA route):
- 5/30: Redwood shares draft IDTA and subprocessor map (today).
- 6/1–6/3: Redwood runs subprocessor scans + TIAs and circulates results.
- 6/4–6/11: MedTech legal redline window.
- 6/14: Execute (DocuSign) and align operational routing.

If Procurement prefers to avoid an IDTA, we can discuss mitigations (e.g., contractual representations + technical routing to EU-only regions) but there are some practical gaps for UK-resident data.

I've attached the two files above. If helpful, we can schedule a short call with our compliance engineer to walk the subprocessor findings.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

(attachments: uk-idta-draft.docx; redwood_subprocessor_map.csv)

Hi all — I reviewed Redwood's draft IDTA and have a few limited redlines focused on: scope of processing, subprocessors and the notification timing for new subprocessors (we prefer 30 days notice and a right to object clause).

Key points:
- Please confirm whether Redwood will commit to routing UK-origin production traffic to UK/EU regions only while the IDTA is pending. We recommend that as an interim technical control.
- Clarify the standard of review for TIAs and whether MedTech gets a summary report (we ask for a 1–2 page summary per TIA).
- Suggest adding a signer block for MedTech's Head of Procurement (procurement@medtechinc.com) on the final page — Procurement needs to be looped.

I can provide tracked redlines if you want; I attached a short cover memo and a marked-up excerpt of the IDTA (cover_memo_idta_redlines.pdf).

Claire O'Connor
